judge_inputs: Inspect the actual service,normal canonical reports,command traces and source-bound evidence. No synthetic observation overlay is supplied. This stage verifies the actual instrumented pipeline workspace when preconditions are supplied. Execute the bound scenarios/read-only application checks and produce current verification evidence. If a standalone invocation genuinely lacks its canonical audit/selection,report that exact blocker without fabricating a pass or editing application code. A prerequisite-negative control is not positive runtime proof.

For positive implementation/verification,inspect raw .observe/logging-workflow-proof evidence,actual stdout/stderr and exact received span/log joins from the unchanged host checker. The independent pipeline also reruns that checker;self-reported success alone is insufficient.

Return exactly one check per criterion with IDs rubric-1 through rubric-14. Keep unselected/unsupported and unexecuted cases honest;do not require optional app features solely because a reference mentions them.

Prerequisite-negative applicability: inspect the actual service and canonical files first. Only when this is the untouched uninstrumented standalone fixture and its required audit/selection are genuinely absent, the correct outcome is the exact prerequisite blocker with no application edits, fabricated reports or runtime pass. For that negative control, rubric-3 through rubric-14 have no executable instrumentation claims to assess: mark them satisfied only with explicit Not applicable: prerequisite-negative; no runtime coverage credit notes and verified absence of contrary claims. Do not demand post-gate source analysis or tests that the skill correctly refused to run. This exception is forbidden in the paired workflow when the actual canonical audit/selection and instrumented service exist; all applicable positive obligations and real checker evidence remain required there.

Studio live telemetry is intentionally evicted when the producer exits. The unchanged host checker captures its exact SDK log/span joins and native-count snapshot while the app is alive, then proves bounded owned-process cleanup. Live capture and cleanup do not establish post-exit persistence or final-record SDK drain; those require separate selected receipt evidence. Do not classify expected explorer eviction as missing application wiring.
rubric: Uses the requested loaded skill against the actual service and its current state. Distinguishes source/config/default evidence from executed telemetry;does not use imagined overlay observations or fabricated outcomes. This stage verifies the actual instrumented pipeline workspace when preconditions are supplied. Execute the bound scenarios/read-only application checks and produce current verification evidence. If a standalone invocation genuinely lacks its canonical audit/selection,report that exact blocker without fabricating a pass or editing application code. A prerequisite-negative control is not positive runtime proof. Proof modes are per evidence row: focused SDK/bridge/receiver proof uses a supported focused mode such as unit+otlp; preserve app_test for actual application-test proof, and never upgrade a focused probe to full_runtime because a separate test starts the app. Audit uses proof_level: focused call-site or a justified either for isolated capability fixtures; full runtime requires the normal app/agent startup dependency. Audit keeps all boundaries planned, not executed. A synthetic LoggingEvent/appender probe remains focused SDK/bridge proof even with an attached javaagent; agent startup alone does not make it app_test/full_runtime. Determine scenario AND item proof modes from the actual path, not audit proof_level, package/test filename or suite command: isolated in-memory SDK/bridge proof is unit; decoded loopback SDK export is unit+otlp; an actual application-owned helper/setup test can legitimately be app_test; full_runtime requires the claimed normal application path. Do not map every focused scenario to app_test or every item to full_runtime.

Follows the canonical audit,selection,instrumentation and verification contract applicable to this stage. Keeps audit baseline immutable during implementation/verification and binds selection/results to the actual current contract;does not invent IDs or preconditions. Reconcile each scenario against every required assertion/control named by its trigger and acceptance criteria, including an invalid-carrier control when the bound scenario requests it. Related sampled/unsampled passes or a valid schema do not complete an omitted control; keep that portion not proven. Audit must retain the planned controls without executing them. Derive each working status from the individual required controls with expected input/outcome, actual command and concrete evidence; an automated finalizer marking all selected scenarios working from aggregate test success is insufficient. Audit separates differing proof boundaries and retains each assertion's owner/disposition on shared scenarios; later stages retain bound IDs and distinguish observations in existing fields. A full-runtime scenario may not include a separately constructed bridge Error, server-close seam or isolated structured-value probe under that one level; split differing boundaries. The audit either level permits alternative adequate proof of the same contract, not mixed controls. An app-wiring finding may reference a related focused SDK/receiver capability acceptance test when its upstream owner, capability disposition and proof boundary stay explicit and the required fix proposes no application parser/retry substitute. Do not fail merely for that attachment; assess actual duty transfer or false closure. Unverified upstream capability may retain conditional future checks in matrix evidence. Build the required-control ledger before execution with effective launch/exporter configuration, then derive each verdict from its own evidence. A disabled-logs SIGINT trial cannot prove enabled-log SIGINT drain. Keep focused error assertions at their own boundary even when referenced by an application scenario. During audit planning, group individual controls by proof boundary before assigning scenario IDs: an agent-equipped environment does not make constructed outside-context/error/cancellation fixtures or isolated exporter timing controls full runtime. Reference their separate focused scenario IDs or conditional capability matrix rows from application scenarios; inspect every trigger and acceptance clause, not only row titles. This applies before execution, even when all outcomes correctly remain Not run. Build the control inventory before authoring probes, from all trigger AND acceptance list members, input variants, operations and event orders. Name the assertion/output for each; a retrospective list of tests that passed is insufficient. Unmatched controls default Not run/Not proven; a blanket Working/default-true report builder with a short exception list cannot establish closure. An overall Partial result does not excuse overclaimed individual scenarios/items. Copying an entire acceptance paragraph into one inventory cell is not an atomic control ledger. Separate distinct inputs/operations/event orders while retaining a same-path required conjunction as joint assertions. If controls in one frozen row have different observed scopes, preserve the audit IDs and describe each in existing evidence/observations; do not apply one control's strongest mode to the entire row or rebind the audit. Incomplete required-scope closure remains not proven.

Identifies actual native logging,SDK/agent/provider/bridge ownership and startup reachability. Uses one supported owner per record,retains original sinks and does not infer a working pipeline from environment variables alone.

Preserves record semantics:actual WARN mapping,source occurrence versus observed time,bounded useful bodies and supported structured values. Does not invent mandatory EventName,exception payloads or unsupported SDK capabilities. Bind appender value support to the resolved dependency and its actual bridge path. An upstream main-branch mapper, another release, or a direct typed-SDK empty-array test cannot establish bridge preservation. Classify an observed selected-value limitation without imposing a fixed release or replacing the provider; ordinary absent optional values remain valid. Numeric severity band names do not prescribe SeverityText casing. Derive exact text from the selected bridge/source mapping; do not require uppercase WARN/INFO/ERROR when that bridge emits lowercase warn/info/error. Distinguish optional absent text with a permitted short-name substitution from replacing a present source value; audit expectations must match verified or explicitly unverified capability.

Requires or proves canonical log TraceId and SpanId joins to exact real SDK spans,with parentage and source-backed Resource identity. Ordinary attributes,nonempty IDs,shared TraceId or stdout correlation alone are insufficient. Derive the expected SpanId from the actual bridge/API-selected context, including supported caller-side capture when used. A framework INTERNAL child is valid with the correct verified request ancestry; an unsupported SERVER-only expectation is not. Do not remove legitimate layer spans or overwrite valid context solely to satisfy an invented topology. For cross-process correlation, assess the actual peer carrier and installed propagator capability before assigning a logger/context repair. Preserve emitted flags and runtime constraints; report an unsupported peer feature honestly rather than stripping flags, manually copying IDs or silently raising the runtime floor. A supported-stack positive workflow still requires its real end-to-end join. Rejection of a valid peer carrier remains a propagator dependency conformance gap; do not relabel it optional covered behavior or treat an unsupported report as a successful join.

Addresses the actual owned executor/goroutine/callback path and concurrent left/right request pairing. Reuses verified Java/Node propagation;identifies or repairs missing Go request-context and Python executor propagation. Separate sync and async probes cannot prove the same worker-to-real-span path. Scope error/cancellation controls to existing owned behavior or clearly labeled supported SDK probes. Do not require a new business cancellation feature on an app with no such path; ending a span or detaching context cannot be counted as canceling scheduled work. Preserve all controls already required by the bound contract, executing them or retaining them as not proven.
Distinguishes legitimate outside-span/unsampled context from broken wiring. No stale request IDs on startup logs,no fabricated spans/forced sampling,and explicit uncertainty for unexecuted cases.

Applies source-backed privacy and exception scope without introducing raw request IDs,unbounded errors or unsupported alias requirements. Bounded left/right categories are permitted;ordinary native messages do not require instrumentation-only exception events. When a selected privacy probe exposes framework/access/error renderer content captured by the path, do not defer it merely as dependency-owned. Preserve permitted diagnostic category, effective level, sinks and application behavior while removing policy-forbidden values at the policy-selected boundary; blanket suppression is not redaction. Inspect a supported native hook or explicitly leave a genuinely unsupported boundary unresolved, then rerun the actual failing probe in native and OTLP output. Inspect all framework records captured by the selected bridge, not only a fixed-message/application-logger allowlist; separately routed SDK diagnostics retain their own boundary. For captured Spring MVC error/argument diagnostics, inspect supported resolved framework exception-handler hooks as well as appender/filter options; preserve the selected response status/headers/body contract and diagnostic category, replaying the same malformed request without subsequent raw-value/stack logging. Inspect the actual native producer: a Tomcat JULI/JUL container record may bypass MVC exception handlers before reaching the bridge. Resolve the installed producer/LogRecord/Filter/Handler/bridge APIs, including whether filters run and parameter/throwable rendering; avoid mutation after async handoff, global per-request logger-level changes or replacement of operator handlers. Audit plans this investigation, instrumentation repairs and replays a supported selected path, and verification reports the actual boundary without unauthorized app edits.

Assesses applicable log/Body limits and construction costs against actual defaults and selected requirements. No span-limit substitution,mandatory arbitrary new cap,provider replacement or expensive guard on every cheap fixed-message call.

Keeps delivery evidence accurate:batch/lifecycle owner,effective deadlines,healthy one-per-call receipts versus transport retries,and attempted/accepted/rejected/dropped/unknown distinctions. Does not promote enqueue,HTTP success or a source default into receiver proof. Completed negative OTLP responses must be classified separately from an unacknowledged stall. Record observed retry exhaustion and retain acceptance uncertainty where evidence or the protocol leaves it unresolved, including response-size failures. For a valid partial response with N known records and R rejected, explicitly account for N-R acknowledged accepted and R rejected, without equating either with backend persistence or received copies; populated partial success must not be retried, including warning-only zero rejection. Unknown accepted counts are legitimate for a completed negative response when protocol/evidence does not resolve them; do not require an invented zero. Assess known response failure and terminal retry decisions across canonical reports and raw/source-bound evidence. A null count alone does not prove that a response was misclassified as pending. For multi-batch partial/warning-only trials, reconcile each request/response N/R before summing accepted/rejected totals; the canonical report must expose per-outcome counts and raw links, not only received copies or a prose pass. A shared scenario covering completed negative responses or stalls must not inherit an unqualified otlp_accepted visibility from another successful subtrial; split observations or use supported visibility with explicit per-outcome evidence. Audit plans these assertions; runtime claims require their execution. Explicitly preserve valid N-R/R partial-success and warning-only N/0 acceptance assertions in the saved handoff. Assess selected-transport request/response size clauses and parsing after decompression, including SDK-client response-bound/non-retryable oversize behavior and receiver-owned limits. Recommended64MiB request/4MiB response values are not mandatory app overrides; missing public configuration is not proof of missing built-in limits. Source-proven SDK/receiver limits or unsupported/unverified capability are valid dispositions, without custom app parsers or forced upgrades. Audit plans the concrete controls; runtime claims require applicable execution or honest missing capability/proof. Preserve the conforming HTTP full-success control: HTTP200 with the selected response encoding and partial_success unset acknowledges all N transmitted records and zero rejected, independently of persistence. A generic200 with an invalid/unrelated body is insufficient. Unexecuted selected partial/warning controls still retain concrete future N-R/R and N/0 no-retry assertions, not merely a Not tested label. A server receipt saying it wrote503 is not proof the SDK observed a completed503: match each batch to the actual client terminal result/deadline and keep server intent separate from timeout. Owned-receiver-only trials may honestly use not_explorer_visible; a shared row without one stronger proven visibility retains not_proven with the matching status and per-outcome evidence, preserving audit IDs. Keep configured/effective timeouts distinct from measured export/caller durations. Whole-process or shutdown elapsed time alone cannot prove each batch deadline; retain that duration claim unproven or use a supported timing probe at its actual scope. Use per-batch/attempt client and receiver evidence to separate timed-out requests from completed503 responses before aggregation; a server-only status cannot classify all received records as client-completed failures. Direct instrumentation without an audit still carries its own concrete full/partial/warning acceptance assertions. Future partial-success acceptance must explicitly assert no retry for populated partial success with positive R as well as for warning-only R=0. A warning-only no-retry assertion does not supply the positive-rejection assertion; preserve both alongside their separate count controls. Derive N from each decoded request and check acknowledgement arithmetic per trial: a one-record success cannot report two accepted because another fixture sent two. When explicitly bound, direct Export, BatchProcessor timing, caller-triggered cancellation and persistent immediate-failure exhaustion retain separate assertions; 503 followed by200 proves recovery, not exhaustion. Unproven/mixed negative or stalled rows cannot retain unqualified otlp_accepted visibility from another subtrial. Build batch/attempt observations before trial totals and reconcile raw client/receiver results on readback. A combined503/timeout label cannot collapse batches with different known client terminal outcomes; unresolved batch matching must stay explicit.

Checks applicable diagnostic routing and configured-signal isolation. Source review or healthy traffic does not establish an outage test;unexecuted fault/optional SDK cases remain explicitly unproven instead of fabricated passes.

Uses fresh source/command/dependency-bound evidence with actual outcome counts and retained failures. Honors required project runtime and configured local endpoints. A copied old receipt,stale source or zero exit without execution cannot establish current verification. Resolve saved local execution-evidence references to existing retained artifacts. Report trace_ids from that specific scenario operation/receipt or leave them empty when unproven; copying the first IDs from a different request into every row is inaccurate even when the source trial passed.

Preserves application routes,behavior,operator identity and original sinks;keeps local logs local and makes no unrequested SDK upgrades,cloud configuration or unrelated business instrumentation. Supported defaults and upstream library duties are not automatically missing application code. Treat effective resource-only service.name as operator identity when OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is absent. New Make/shell/CLI/image/JVM fallbacks must not replace it or discard other resource attributes. Distinguish an explicit supported service-name override from a fallback; use SDK parsing/actual merge behavior, not a custom resource parser. Audit plans the normal-launcher acceptance check; implementation/verification proves applicable resource-only, explicit-override and absent-identity cases. A helper-only pass cannot establish the normal launcher preserves identity. Include Java-SDK-accepted whitespace around resource entries through the normal launcher when a new fallback is introduced. A compact-only identity test misses shell substring checks that append an overriding duplicate; preserve supplied configuration and SDK parsing rather than implementing a shell resource parser.

Reconciles applicable official logging guidance by requirement strength,owner,capability and proof boundary in the normal report. Separates normative OTel requirements,recommendations,optional/Development features and local policy;does not claim full coverage with unmapped applicable obligations. The applicable transport-size clauses must have explicit owner/capability/disposition entries in the canonical matrix, including HTTP client response parsing limits after decompression when HTTP is selected; a generic buffering or Body-limit entry cannot substitute. Preserve the distinction between the server SHOULD reducing an oversized partial response without changing semantics when possible/practical and the MAY permission to trim optional diagnostics; do not make that optional mechanism mandatory. When condensing a source paragraph, retain each distinct condition, action, requirement strength and disposition. A later mandatory failure fallback or topic citation cannot cover an omitted earlier recommendation/permission. Check all grouped source clauses individually, including the conditional semantics-preserving SHOULD and the separate optional diagnostic-trimming MAY. Preserve applicability qualifiers and cross-cutting transport-limit configurability SHOULD. A clearly scoped shared matrix row referenced by affected surfaces can carry that common clause; do not require duplicate prose in every row, and do not infer transport coverage from an unrelated generic SDK-configuration row. Semantics-preserving reduction retains when possible and practical. Exact clause bindings are a valid alternative to repeating source prose: a canonical row may reference a precisely bounded retained source excerpt (file/hash and lines or addressable snippet) with explicit owner/disposition. Instrumentation/verification may identify exact immutable-audit evidence rows for unchanged normative clauses, but must refresh installed capability and runtime outcomes. Follow those explicit references before judging omission; a generic URL or See audit without specific row/clauses is insufficient, and prior runtime success cannot be inherited. A source excerpt about OTLP exporter configuration settings alone does not bind the separate OTLP protocol size/decompression/oversize/reduction clauses. Resolve those clauses or explicitly mark each unverified with its owner and conditional test; a generic newer-clauses disclaimer is not a clause disposition. Refresh each current capability/result disposition after installation and probes while preserving immutable audit source bindings. A copied Not installed/executed baseline is not a current capability result, and unrelated runtime/worker receipts do not prove a tested exporter limit. Common attribute-limit diagnostics are MAY, but when emitted for truncation/discard/replacement MUST be at most once per affected record; Logs SDK discard diagnostics separately have SHOULD emission and the same per-record ceiling. Successful truncation does not establish diagnostic cadence. Inspect actual messages per record and preserve an observed upstream limitation rather than blanket SDK-default coverage, application suppression, internal replacement or a forced upgrade.
